This basically follows how we managed it last year, except now they’re separating Origination and Portfolio teams. Regarding Assistants – we need to set their bonus targets rather than letting Compensation just decide. For non-investment staff – again, we need to define targets (as we discussed earlier this week).

The biggest challenge remains how to integrate Atlas and avoid the manual Atlas-spreadsheet-Atlas cycle we had last year. We’re collaborating with Hannah Ferguson and the Atlas team on this.

VPs have to go through the final firm-wide Charlotte review, so that adds a step for the VPs, and the Portfolio Ops meeting results should align with how all employees are rated heading into the final session (i.e., 10/80/10, scale 1-100).

Jennifer
</body>

Here is our plan on Charlotte.

Assistants:

Ranked 1,2,3 by supervisors - pay determined by me and Brandy.  No meetings.

Karen Smith but in Raleigh:

Traditional ranking with the right people attending the meetings.  Pay grid set by Compensation.

Analysts and Associates

Ranked as per Kenneth Winters’ percentages and then pay grid set by Compensation.
I’d prefer a 25% - 65% - 10% split. Kenneth disagrees. This would allow a quick meeting rather than splitting into 4 groups where the top excludes some strong performers.

Managers/Directors

Ranked 1 to 100 in clusters as seen fit. We’re combining managers and directors into one table. Rankings based on this year’s performance directly linked to pay. Two meetings – one for portfolio managers and one for support teams (Origination/Finance/etc). No pay committee, but we’ll use ranking results and work with leaders post-meeting to finalize compensation.

We’ll also decide promotions at this meeting using different criteria.

VPs

All VPs ranked 1 to 100 by a selected group – some VPs and some MDs.
This will also be directly linked to pay.

Cheers as you Brits say
